answers.explanation: Average power is the gain in kinetic energy per time: (½ × 800 × 25²)/20 = 1.25 × 10^4 W.
Momentum is conserved; the combined mass moves at 0.05 × 200/1.00 = 10 m/s, giving kinetic energy ½ × 1 × 10² = 50 J.
Total mechanical energy is conserved: ½mv² + mgh = ½ × 0.1 × 10² + 0.1 × 10 × 10 = 15 J.
The movable pulley is supported by two equal rope tensions, so 2W = 40 N and W = 20 N.
A body topples when the vertical line through its centre of gravity falls outside its base of support.
Force is proportional to mass × acceleration; the ratio is (3 × 2):(1 × 9) = 2:3.
Acceleration = 80/20 = 4 m/s²; retardation = 80/(90 − 50) = 2 m/s².
Centripetal force = mrω² = 0.01 × 0.2 × 100² = 20 N.
The internal diameter of a small test tube is measured accurately with vernier calipers.
At constant temperature Boyle's law gives P₁V₁ = P₂V₂; reducing volume to one-fifth makes pressure 5P₀.
Equating lost gravitational potential energy to heat, mgh = mcΔT; ΔT = gh/c = 10 × 20/450 = 4/9 °C.
On the downward stroke, the piston valve P opens to let water pass above the piston, while lower valve Q closes.
The added 15 cm Hg raises the trapped-air pressure from 75 to 90 cm Hg; Boyle's law gives V₂ = 30 × 75/90 = 25 cm³.
Upthrusts are 4 N in water and 3 N in liquid X; relative density = 3/4.
Boiling occurs when saturated vapour pressure equals external pressure; solutes and increased external pressure raise the boiling point. I, II and III are correct.
Surface tension decreases as the temperature of a liquid increases.
During braking, friction acts opposite the car's motion and helps bring it to rest, so it is an advantage.
The mirror is 3 m from the man after moving; the image is 3 m behind it, so the man-image distance is 6 m.
Sound speed increases in hotter air while frequency remains constant; since λ = v/f, wavelength increases.
In y = A sin(500t − 0.025x), the angular frequency is the coefficient of t, 500 rad/s.
Copper releases Q = mcΔT = 2 × 400 × 100 = 80000 J; melted ice mass = 80000/(3.3 × 10^5) = 8/33 kg.
The diagram shows three complete wavelengths in 0.3 m, so λ = 0.1 m and f = v/λ = 3.0 × 10^9 Hz.
Temperature gradient = (80 − 20)/0.02 = 3.0 × 10^3 K/m.
As the south pole moves from P towards Q, induction makes P a south pole and Q a north pole.
Identical cells in parallel retain an e.m.f. of 1.5 V and have equivalent internal resistance 4/4 = 1 Ω.
The same emf gives 5(8 + X) = 7(5 + X); solving yields X = 2.5 Ω.
A telescope is in normal adjustment when its final image is at infinity.
Steel has greater retentivity than iron, so it retains magnetism more strongly and is suitable for permanent magnets.
The prism arrangement shown is used in a periscope to redirect the line of sight.
Snell's law gives sin i = (3.0/2.0) sin 30° = 0.75.
The resistor and inductor voltage drops are at right angles; supply voltage = √(6² + 8²) = 10 V.
Laminating the transformer core reduces eddy currents and therefore reduces the heat they produce.
In Fleming's right-hand rule, the thumb indicates motion, the forefinger the magnetic field, and the middle finger induced current.
The capacitors are in parallel, so Ctotal = 2 + 3 = 5 μF; energy = ½CV² = ½ × 5 × 10^-6 × 100² = 2.5 × 10^-2 J.
Inductive reactance XL = 2πfL; f = 2000/(2π × 10) = 100/π Hz.
The cooker current is I = P/V = 3000/200 = 15 A; the suitable listed fuse is 20 A.
The galvanometer current is the shunt current multiplied by Rs/Rg: 2 × 0.05/5 = 0.02 A = 20 mA.
Both resistors have the same potential difference; P₁/P₂ = (V²/R₁)/(V²/R₂) = R₂/R₁.
